parsed.wine_summary:
Black Box is the dominant brand in premium boxed wine in the U.S., and the Deep & Dark Cabernet Sauvignon is their play for consumers who want something bolder than their standard Cab. At 3 liters per box (equivalent to four bottles), the format keeps wine fresh for up to six weeks after opening thanks to the vacuum-sealed bag-in-box design, which eliminates oxidation far better than a recorked bottle.

The wine sources fruit from across California's Central Valley and warmer inland regions, where Cabernet Sauvignon ripens reliably to high sugar levels, producing the dense, fruit-forward style the label promises. The 2021 vintage clocks in at 13.0% ABV — moderate for California Cab — suggesting the winemaking team is pulling fruit before it gets jammy, or blending to keep alcohol in check. Competition medals (including a Gold for 2022) confirm this performs well in blind tastings against its price tier, which is the relevant benchmark.

The heat drives rapid sugar accumulation and produces thick-skinned berries with concentrated dark fruit character and soft acid. Cooling influence is minimal compared to coastal California, so you won't find the herbal, green pepper notes of cooler-climate Cab — instead, expect ripe blackberry and plum with low-to-moderate natural acidity, which is exactly what the 'Deep & Dark' name telegraphs.
